desc:
The strings low and high are decimal integers with low ≤ high. Count the integers x with low ≤ x ≤ high whose digit sum lies between minSum and maxSum inclusive. The digit sum of x is the sum of its decimal digits.

The count can be huge, so return it modulo 109 + 7.

Example: low = "1", high = "12", minSum = 1, maxSum = 8: the numbers 1 to 8 qualify, as do 10 (sum 1), 11 (sum 2) and 12 (sum 3), while 9 (sum 9) does not. The answer is 11.
constraints: 1 ≤ low ≤ high ≤ 10<sup>100</sup> - 1; both strings have at most 100 digits and no leading zeros
hints: Counting by looping over the range is impossible with up to 100 digits. Think of a number as a string of digits and count strings instead.
Let F(s, T) be the number of integers in [0, s] with digit sum at most T. Then the count for the range is a combination of F(high, ...) and F(low, ...) with a correction for low itself.

To compute F: precompute ways[len][t], the number of digit strings of length len (leading zeros allowed) with digit sum at most t. Then scan s from the left: at each position, for every digit smaller than s[i] add ways[remaining][T - prefixSum - digit], and continue along the digits of s itself.
editorial: This is a digit DP. First tabulate exact[l][t]: the number of length-l digit strings (leading zeros allowed) with digit sum exactly t. It satisfies exact[l][t] = sum of exact[l-1][t-d] over digits d = 0..9, which a prefix sum evaluates in O(1) per cell. Taking prefix sums over t gives ways[l][t], the number of strings with sum at most t.

Define F(s, T) as the number of integers in [0, s] with digit sum ≤ T (0 if T < 0). Walk along s: at position i with prefix digit sum pre, every smaller digit d at this position makes the rest free, contributing ways[n-i-1][T - pre - d] when that index is not negative. Then follow the digit s[i] itself; if pre exceeds T, stop; if the whole string is traversed within the limit, s itself counts +1.

The number of qualifying integers up to s is G(s) = F(s, maxSum) - F(s, minSum - 1). The answer is G(high) - G(low) plus 1 if low itself qualifies (since G(high) - G(low) excludes it). All arithmetic is modulo 109+7. The table has about 100 × 900 cells and each query scans at most 100 × 10 states.
